newsitem.title: UK: UK's Social Chapter opt-out aids jobless fall - govt.
newsitem.headline: UK's Social Chapter opt-out aids jobless fall - govt.

text.p: Britain's deputy prime minister Michael Heseltine said Britain's opt-out from the European Union Social Chapter on workers' rights was one of the main reasons for its record of falling unemployment.

"Unemployment in Britain is low and falling," he told a news conference. "Almost everywhere else in the European Union it is high and rising. Even our worst regions now have unemployment comparable with Germany's best."
Heseltine said the obvious lesson was that Britain was benefiting from flexible and deregulated labour market policies introduced by the Conservative government.
"Fundamental to our success is the opt-out from the Social Chapter achieved by the Prime Minister at Maastricht. If our success is to be maintained, that opt-out must be maintained."
Britain's jobless total fell 68,200 to 1.75 million in February, leaving 6.2 percent of the working population without a job.

Heseltine said the opposition Labour party's plans to sign up to the Social Chapter and to introduce a national minimum wage "would force all the restrictions of the European social model onto Britain, putting countless jobs at risk."
